subtopic: The Modulus and the Conjugate of a Complex Number
title: Conjugate properties

board_content.text: What the conjugate does to sums and products
Adding a number to its conjugate kills the imaginary part; subtracting kills the real part.
Multiplying a number by its mirror image gives a non-negative real — the squared distance.

board_content.latex: \overline{z_1 z_2}=\bar z_1\,\bar z_2,\qquad \overline{z_1\pm z_2}=\bar z_1\pm\bar z_2

board_content.text: $\overline{z_1 z_2}=\bar z_1\bar z_2$ — a product, NOT $\bar z_1+\bar z_2$.
Likewise the conjugate of a quotient is the quotient of conjugates, and $\overline{z^{n}}=(\bar z)^{n}$.

segments_english.text: The conjugate has a small toolkit of properties that make it powerful. Let's walk through them.
First, conjugating twice returns you to z. Adding z and its conjugate gives two times the real part. Subtracting gives two i times the imaginary part.
Read that intuitively: adding a number to its mirror image cancels the up-down parts and leaves twice the horizontal, while subtracting cancels the horizontal and leaves the vertical.
Now the star property: z times z bar equals a squared plus b squared, which is the modulus of z, squared.

This is magical because a complex times its mirror image produces a plain, non-negative real number, exactly the squared distance from the origin. That's the trick behind every division and every proof of realness.
Conjugation also plays nicely with operations: the conjugate of a product is the product of conjugates, and the conjugate of a sum or difference splits across the terms.
Watch the trap here: the conjugate of a product is z one bar times z two bar. It is a product of conjugates, not a sum of them.
And it extends: the conjugate of a quotient is the quotient of the conjugates, and the conjugate of a power is that power of the conjugate.

segments_hinglish.text: Conjugate ke paas properties ka ek chhota toolkit hai jo ise powerful banata hai. Chalo inpe chalte hain.
Pehle, do baar conjugate karne se wapas z mil jaata hai. z aur uske conjugate ko add karne se milta hai two times real part. Subtract karne se milta hai two i times imaginary part.

Ise intuitively padho: kisi number ko uske mirror image se add karne par up-down parts cancel ho jaate hain aur twice horizontal bachta hai, jabki subtract karne par horizontal cancel aur vertical bachta hai.
Ab star property: z times z bar barabar a square plus b square, jo hai modulus of z, squared.

Ye magical hai kyunki ek complex apne mirror image se multiply hoke ek plain, non-negative real number banata hai, theek origin se squared distance. Yehi trick hai har division aur har realness proof ke peeche.
Conjugation operations ke saath achhe se chalti hai: product ka conjugate hai conjugates ka product, aur sum ya difference ka conjugate terms par split ho jaata hai.
Yahan trap dekho: product ka conjugate hai z one bar times z two bar. Ye conjugates ka product hai, unka sum nahi.
Aur ye extend hota hai: quotient ka conjugate hai conjugates ka quotient, aur power ka conjugate hai conjugate ki wahi power.
